hook: Andrew Barto earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics and a PhD in computer and communication sciences, both from the University of Michigan. In 1977 he joined the University of Massachusetts Amherst as a postdoctoral research associate and spent his career there, rising through associate professor and professor to department chair before becoming Professor Emeritus of Information and Computer Sciences. Beginning in the 1980s, working closely with Richard Sutton, he developed the conceptual and algorithmic foundations of reinforcement learning, including temporal difference learning, policy gradient methods and agent designs that combine learning with planning. He and Sutton distilled that work into the textbook Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, first published in 1998 with a second edition in 2018, which became the standard reference for the field. In 2024 the Association for Computing Machinery awarded Barto and Sutton the ACM A.M. Turing Award for this body of work.
